headline: Approved Autumn Crabtree as secretary; discussed low turnout at Comprehensive Plan open house and ways to reach more residents.
summary: Members discussed low turnout and limited public feedback at the Economic Vitality open house. They talked about outreach ideas, including plain language, translation, and surveys shared through community groups and local businesses. Members also approved the previous meeting minutes.

plain_text:
8/18/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Brittany Nevins, Alejandra Lopez, Autumn Crabtree
City Staff Present: Angela Aldieri, Elsie Goodrich
Guests Present: None
Call to Order by: Brittany Nevins
Meeting Start Time: 6:02pm
Minutes Recorded by Angela Aldieri
Public Comment
There were no members of the public present.
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Autumn Crabtree
Second: Alejandra Lopez
Decision: Approved
City Council Liaison Update
Councilor Goodrich thanked the commission for adjusting their schedule for the election last 
week. She went on to note that 24% of registered voters participated compared to 14% in 2024 
and there were 81 new voter registration on election day. Councilor Goodrich highlighted Council 
action taken on a MOU with Downtown Winooski and new and updated position descriptions at 
their most recent meeting.
Inclusion & Belonging Commission Update
There was no member of the Inclusion & Belonging Commission present.
Approve: Commission Officers
Secretary
Motion by: Alejandra Lopez 
Second: Brittany Nevins
Decision: Approved
Notes: Autumn Crabtree volunteered to serve as secretary at future meetings.
Discussion: Comprehensive Plan Open House Debrief
The Commission discussed the low turnout and limited public feedback received at the 
Economic Vitality open house. Discussion ensued regarding the challenges of conducting 
outreach without a dedicated staff person; whether separate meetings for each section are the 
best approach; and opportunities to reach a broader audience through combined sessions, 
varied meeting times, informal events, existing community gatherings, and local organizations. 
The greater participation at the Municipal Infrastructure open house was also discussed.
Emphasis was placed on making outreach accessible and intentional, including engaging non-
English speakers, new Americans, young professionals, businesses, and others who may not 
typically participate in City meetings. Members also discussed the use of plain language, 
translation services, passive opportunities for feedback, and making surveys available through 
community organizations and local businesses. The Commission noted that the 
Comprehensive Plan is updated every eight years pursuant to state statute and is due for 
renewal in March 2027, and expressed a desire for greater opportunities for public input given 
the plan's eight-year life. It was noted that Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning, has 
been connected with Melissa Corbin of Downtown Winooski to solicit input from the business 
community regarding the Economic Vitality section.
Other Business
There was no other business discussed
Adjourn
Motion by: Autumn Crabtree
Second: Brittany Nevins
Meeting End Time: 6:41pm
